About me

I’m Mohamed Khalil Ibrahim, a Data Analyst and BI Developer passionate about transforming complex data into meaningful insights that drive smarter business decisions. With 3 years of hands-on experience in data analytics and business intelligence projects, I specialize in uncovering trends, identifying business opportunities, and translating data into actionable strategies.

My expertise spans SQL, Python, Excel, and Power BI, with a strong focus on data cleaning, exploratory data analysis, data modeling, KPI development, and interactive dashboard creation. I combine analytical thinking with business understanding to turn raw data into clear, reliable, and decision-ready information.

I believe data analysis is not just about numbers and reports; it’s about creating measurable business value. My goal is to help organizations understand their performance, optimize operations, identify growth opportunities, reduce inefficiencies, and make confident, data-driven decisions.

Featured projects

Selected work, from SQL analysis to full dashboards. Figures come from each project’s screenshots and my CV.

Superstore Sales Dashboard (Excel)

Excel, pivot tables, slicers

Objective
Show sales, profit and category performance from the Superstore dataset in one interactive Excel dashboard.
Tools
Excel pivot tables, slicers, dynamic charts and a data model
Key findings
  • About $2.3M in sales and $286K profit, a 12.46% margin
  • The West region contributes 31% of total sales
  • Year-over-year sales growth of 24.62%, 32.53% and 14.20% for 2015 to 2017
  • 793 customers averaging 6 orders each
  • Top and lowest five products by sales ranked side by side

Brazilian E-Commerce (Olist) Analysis

Power BI, DAX, Data modeling

Objective
Track revenue, order value and customer behavior for a Brazilian online marketplace, by period, category and city.
Tools
Power BI, DAX, Power Query, star-schema model (sales fact with product, seller, customer and date dimensions)
Key findings
  • About 17M in revenue from 99K orders and 96K customers
  • Average order value of 168, with 1.2 items per order
  • Repeat customer rate is only 3%
  • São Paulo leads city revenue at 2.3M, followed by Rio de Janeiro at 1.2M
  • Health and beauty is the top category, ahead of watches and gifts
View Project

Bank Customer Churn Analysis

Power BI

Objective
Identify the key factors affecting customer retention and visualize churn trends so the bank can target retention efforts.
Tools
Power BI, DAX
Key findings
  • 10K customers, 2,037 churned: a 20.37% churn rate
  • Value of lost customers estimated at $206.69M
  • Germany has the highest churn rate at 32.44%, against 16.67% in Spain and 16.15% in France
  • Customers holding a single product account for 1,409 of the churned customers
  • Female customers make up 60.37% of churn and male customers 39.63%
  • Reduced churn prediction error by 15% by identifying key behavioral patterns
View Project

Sales Transactions Analysis

Power BI, DAX, Power Query

Objective
Analyze a sales transactions dataset to track revenue, order value, product performance and cancellations over time and by region.
Tools
Power BI, DAX measures, Power Query (including a fix for a mixed date format), star schema modeling
Key findings
  • About $63M in revenue from 23K transactions across 3,767 products
  • Average order value of $3K and an average price of $11
  • December has the highest revenue spike, up 19% against November
  • 85% of transactions completed and 15% canceled
  • The top product generates about $1M, 16% of total product revenue
  • The interactive dashboard improved decision-making speed by 25%
View Project
